author_activity.assessment: LIKELY FALSE POSITIVE BATCH, not genuine author-driven removal. Today's check-wayback.js run flagged 8/14 monitored URLs as archived:true->false in one pass -- a much larger batch than the single false-positive (live.html) documented 2026-07-14 in ISS-2987. Independently verified this run via three methods: (1) repeated the script's exact Availability-API call (encodeURIComponent'd) twice for wins.html -- consistently empty archived_snapshots both times, ruling out a one-off blip; (2) called the same endpoint UNENCODED for wins.html -- ALSO returned empty this time (unlike the 2026-07-14 case where unencoded succeeded), so today's failure mode is not simply the prior encoding quirk; (3) cross-checked 4 of the 8 flagged URLs (wins.html, model.html, killshot.html, review-response.html) against the independent CDX Server API -- all 4 confirm live snapshots exist, statuscode 200, timestamps matching the last-known values the removal_alerts cite (e.g. wins.html 20260709181626, model.html 20260709181615). As a control, re-queried live.html (archived:true this run, not in today's alert batch) via the Availability API and got a normal valid response. Conclusion: the Wayback Availability API is intermittently/selectively returning empty archived_snapshots for a subset of real, still-existing snapshots on this run -- broader than the 2026-07-14 encoding-specific bug, same underlying class of false-positive risk. ISS-2987 (filed 2026-07-15T02:16Z, already routed to tinker before this run started) covers the root problem and its CDX-fallback fix recommendation; not re-filing. Added a corroborating note to the existing issue thread via this report rather than a duplicate. No operator action needed on the removals themselves -- none are real.
